newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks storm to record closing high.
newsitem.headline: German stocks storm to record closing high.

text.p: German stocks stormed to a new record high on Friday, supported by ongoing speculation about consolidation in Germany's banking sector.

The blue-chip 30-share DAX index ended floor trade up 42.44 points, establishing a record closing high of 3,604.55, the first time the index has closed above the psychologically important 3,600 level.

At the center of speculation about consolidation in the financial sector was talk that Bankgesellschaft Berlin, fresh from announcing talks of a possible merger with NordLB, might be considering taking on BHF Bank as well. Both sides however said there was nothing to the talk.
BHF finished floor trade up 7.6 percent at 45.90 marks while Bankgesellschaft shares climbed eight percent to 38.60 marks.
Deutsche Bank, meanwhile, shrugged off a downgrade from Credit Suisse to hold from buy to climb 1.80 marks to 98.70 marks.
Shares in utility company Viag AG fell one mark to 770.0 marks after the company announced earnings this year would at least match those seen in 1996.
